mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-20.1 to -13.3), indicating a sustained recovery trend in discretionary mobility that is expected to persist and push the four-week mean higher than the prior four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -20.1 to -13.3 over three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next four-week mean is equal to or lower than the prior four-week mean despite the three-week upward run, the momentum-continuation hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility crosses above -45 (i.e., recovers past a critical restriction-easing threshold), this signals relaxation of transit-related restrictions that enables greater retail footfall, raising RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -45 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -53.6 to -46.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses -45 but RETAIL_REC's two-week-forward mean does not increase relative to the two-week-prior mean, the threshold mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in RESIDENTIAL time (8.1 to 5.1) alongside improving WORKPLACES (-21.3 to -19.1) jointly indicate households re-engaging in out-of-home routines; the combined effect amplifies retail visitation beyond what either series would predict alone, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 8.1 to 5.1 while WORKPLACES rose from -21.3 to -19.1
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL continues falling and WORKPLACES continues rising but RETAIL_REC's four-week mean does not exceed the prior period's mean, the joint-interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility sharply rebounded in the most recent week (-21.9 to -10.9), consistent with seasonal outdoor activity patterns; in a reopening regime this outdoor-engagement surge spills over into nearby retail and recreation visits within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -21.9 to -10.9 in the latest week
failure_condition: If PARKS remains elevated but RETAIL_REC's two-week-forward mean fails to rise relative to its two-week-prior mean, the seasonal spillover hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Short-term co-movement between PARKS and RETAIL_REC in the most recent week (both jumping substantially) suggests a shared single-week behavioral driver (e.g., a long weekend or weather event); this joint spike is expected to persist for one more week before reverting toward trend.
evidence_refs: fact:both PARKS and RETAIL_REC rose sharply in the t-0w week
failure_condition: If the next week's RETAIL_REC mean falls back to or below the t-1w level despite PARKS remaining elevated, the short-term co-movement hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES has stabilized near -19 to -21 for the last three weeks, indicating a steady-state policy regime with no further easing; absent additional workplace reopening, retail recovery will plateau and RETAIL_REC's next four-week mean will not exceed the prior period's mean.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES held between -19.1 and -21.3 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next four-week mean is clearly higher than the prior four-week mean despite WORKPLACES remaining flat, the plateau hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 5.0 (crossing a threshold indicating reduced home-confinement), this signals a behavioral shift toward more out-of-home activity, which will raise RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 5.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 8.1 to 5.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL crosses below 5.0 but RETAIL_REC's two-week-forward mean does not rise relative to its two-week-prior mean, the threshold hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has steadily increased toward positive territory (-1.0 to 0.7), reflecting a seasonal normalization of essential shopping patterns; this baseline-level essential mobility signals broader normalization that will extend to discretionary retail within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -1.0 to 0.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM continues to rise but RETAIL_REC's next one-week mean does not increase relative to the current week, the normalization-spillover hypothesis is rejected.
